resumen: Hands on the edge of a bench beside the hips, and the body goes down and up by bending the elbows. A bodyweight triceps exercise that needs only a bench.
ejecucion: Sit on the edge of a bench and put your hands beside your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Move your hips forward off the bench, with your legs straight, or knees bent to make it easier.
Lower by bending your elbows straight back, without flaring them, until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Push up with your hands until your arms are straight, keeping your hips close to the bench.
matices: A study comparing bench, bar and ring dips found that on the bench the work falls mainly on the triceps, but the shoulder reaches its maximum extension, more than in the other variations. That is why the advice is not to go past upper arms parallel to the floor, and to choose another triceps exercise if the shoulder hurts.

fuentes.titulo: Bench, Bar, and Ring Dips: Do Kinematics and Muscle Activity Differ?
